findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext long-lived credentials. User data is readable via the instance metadata service (including through SSRF), is visible in the EC2 console/API to anyone with DescribeInstanceAttribute, and is stored in cleartext in Terraform state.

The instance is launched into aws_subnet.web_subnet, which sets map_public_ip_on_launch and is associated with a route table routing 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway, while its security group permits 22 and 80 from anywhere. The host is therefore directly reachable from the internet.

No metadata_options block is configured, so token-optional IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with the internet-facing web service and the credentials placed in user data, an SSRF flaw allows trivial retrieval of user data and any role credentials.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device block sets encrypted = true, so the instance root volume may be created unencrypted unless account-level EBS default encryption happens to be on, leaving data at rest unprotected.
Ingress on TCP 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative SSH access on a publicly addressed host to the entire internet for brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the instance serves only plain HTTP (Apache with no TLS configured), so traffic to the host is transmitted in cleartext from an unrestricted source range.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing unconstrained outbound traffic that facilitates data exfiltration and command-and-control from a compromised host.
The EBS volume attached to the web host is created without encrypted = true (the argument is explicitly commented out), so its data at rest is unencrypted.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted volume and no encryption is configured, so snapshot data is stored in cleartext and can be restored or shared without KMS-based access control.
The VPC flow log destination bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so network flow records revealing internal topology and traffic patterns are stored without enforced encryption.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving no defence-in-depth against an ACL or policy change publicly exposing sensitive network logs.
The bucket has no policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so flow log objects may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with the 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway means every instance launched here is automatically internet-reachable, removing a network segmentation boundary.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the same internet-gateway route table cause instances in this subnet to receive public IPs and be directly exposed to the internet.

The VPC's default security group is not managed and locked down with aws_default_security_group, so any resource launched without an explicit security group inherits the default allow-all intra-group ingress and unrestricted egress.
